title: The Next-Generation Computing Framework | World Economic Forum
gist: A WEF/Global Future Council framework scores national and corporate computing strategies on sovereignty and interdependence, cybersecurity and resilience, and sustainability across seven dimensions, citing global computing infrastructure investment of $459 billion in 2025, expected to grow tenfold by 2027.

themes.theme: Computing infrastructure as a policy constraint

insights.claim: Global investment in computing infrastructure reached $459 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow tenfold by 2027.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A tenfold step-up in two years frames the scale of AI/quantum compute capex — and the energy and supply chain demands behind it.

insights.claim: Countries face a complex challenge of securing access to computing power while managing energy demands, geopolitical dependencies and evolving cyberthreats as AI, quantum and other technologies reshape economies.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Compute access is becoming a strategic sovereignty issue, linking energy, geopolitics and cyber risk.

insights.claim: The Next-Generation Computing Framework assesses three pillars — sovereignty and interdependence, cybersecurity and resilience, and sustainability — across seven dimensions, with a scorecard to help decision-makers identify priorities and trade-offs.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Global Future Council on Next Generation Computing
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for comparing national compute strategies and data-center siting trade-offs.
insights.locator: Its framework examines three interconnected pillars

top_entities: Global Future Council on Next Generation Computing
